chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjāl from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl said:

I heard Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'He who leads this House (the Ka‘bah) is of no account if he does not possess three qualities: forbearance by which he controls his anger, good character by which he associates with his companions, and piety which restrains him from the sins of Allah.'

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: The House, referring to the Ka'bah in Mecca.
key_terms.حِلْمٌ: Forbearance or patience, specifically the ability to control one's anger.
key_terms.خُلُقٌ: Character or manners, referring to how one interacts with others.
key_terms.وَرَعٌ: Piety or God-consciousness, specifically restraining oneself from sins.
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: To lead (prayer), referring to the role of the Imam.

ai.seo_question: What are the three essential qualities required for the leader of prayer in the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) defines the spiritual and moral prerequisites for the Imām al-Ṣalāh, emphasizing that leadership in prayer is not merely a ritual role but a position of moral authority. The triad of forbearance (*ḥilm*), amiable character (*khuluq*), and piety (*wara‘*) ensures the leader can guide the congregation with patience, approachability, and strict adherence to divine commands, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on the Imam’s moral exemplarity.
